15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.visual_critic_note: Functional and readable with thoughtful community-color encoding and a useful side bar chart, but schemeCategory10 palette, flat typographic hierarchy, and multicolored row/column labels create visual noise rather than clarity.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.encoding_integrity_note: Bar chart baseline is zero and degree scale uses d3.max for a data-driven domain, but mouseout resets all cell opacity to 1 rather than restoring the fill-opacity weight encoding, permanently erasing the weight signal after any hover.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() before reorder transitions, mouseover force-updates all 1225 cells' opacity on every cell entry, and no touch/mouse event deduplication exists.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.cognitive_load_note: 35×35 matrix with 5 community colors is structurally sound and hover highlighting aids reading, but the default Name ordering scatters community colors into visual noise — the viewer must discover the Community sort button to extract any meaningful structure, and the simultaneous opacity-weight encoding adds a second dimension that compounds the initial confusion.

39-quadtree-hit-detection.visual_critic_note: Dark canvas with Tableau-palette dots, glowing nearest-point highlights, and a clean frosted-glass UI panel make this feel deliberately designed rather than default, though the 8 scattered category colors lack harmony at low density.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.encoding_integrity_note: No deceptive encoding — position and categorical color are used honestly, particle radius is random aesthetic variation not data encoding, and zoom correctly transforms world coordinates via transform.applyX/Y; docked from top marks only because no quantitative axis encoding is present to audit for baseline/lie-factor issues and domains are hardcoded to synthetic world dimensions.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.stress_test_note: Both mousemove and zoom fire full canvas redraws (5000 particles) plus quadtree rebuilds on every event with zero throttling, debouncing, or RAF coalescing; no touch/mouse disambiguation on the D3 zoom+mousemove dual-listener setup risks scroll/zoom fights on mobile.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.cognitive_load_note: Single view with one interaction mode (hover to find 10 nearest), 8-color categorical palette at the warning threshold but interaction dims non-selected points to near-zero, making the active context clear; the main static-screenshot limitation is that the hover-dimming and line-drawing behavior can't be fully assessed without interaction.

53-textured-raincloud.visual_critic_note: Intentional Paul Tol muted palette with redundant texture encoding for colorblind accessibility is genuinely thoughtful, clean card layout and typographic hierarchy are solid, but the chart extends beyond the screenshot viewport leaving groups E and F cut off.
53-textured-raincloud.encoding_integrity_note: Honest raincloud encoding with data-driven x-domain and per-group KDE normalization (standard practice), but hardcoded KDE bandwidth (2.5) would distort shapes under data rescaling, and the Math.max(0,...) x-domain floor silently clips negative values.
53-textured-raincloud.stress_test_note: Essentially static visualization with a single button toggle applying a CSS filter; no brush, zoom, cross-view dispatch, D3 transitions, or touch handlers present, so none of the five interaction robustness failure modes apply.
53-textured-raincloud.cognitive_load_note: Six groups with redundant color+pattern encoding are well-managed and the three-layer raincloud (KDE, box, jitter) reads as a cohesive unit, but the chart extends below the viewport requiring scroll to see all groups, breaking at-a-glance comparison.

68-animated-sparkline-table.visual_critic_note: Clean dashboard layout with intentional color coding (red for offline), varied sparkline types across KPI cards, and good typographic hierarchy — held back from 8 by the win/loss chart using raw green/red bars without visual calibration and the bullet chart's muted gray ranges blending indistinctly.
68-animated-sparkline-table.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baselines are correct on all bar/area charts and domains are data-driven via d3.max, but per-row independent y-scales on table sparklines make cross-row visual magnitude comparison misleading, and no line.defined() guard exists for missing data.
68-animated-sparkline-table.stress_test_note: The Replay button calls animateAll() without .interrupt(), so rapid clicks during a running transition snap elements to width=0 immediately while old transitions may still be queued, causing conflicting animation state; no brush/zoom storms, no feedback loops, no stale closures, and no mouse-touch conflicts are present.
68-animated-sparkline-table.cognitive_load_note: 4 KPI cards + 7-row sparkline table with restrained 2-color palette and clear status badges keep cognitive load low; animation is purposeful (left-to-right wipe with stagger) but cannot be fully evaluated from a static screenshot.

77-sunburst-breadcrumb-brush.visual_critic_note: Clean sunburst layout with soft card shadows, but the rainbow palette (interpolateRainbow) is generic, the breadcrumb trail only shows 'All Products' at rest with no typographic hierarchy, and the chart is cropped at the bottom—cutting off a full quarter of the visualization.
77-sunburst-breadcrumb-brush.encoding_integrity_note: Angular proportional encoding via d3.partition is mathematically correct and data-driven (no magic domains), but the data join lacks key functions which could cause corruption on dynamic updates, and the brush desaturates only visually without actually filtering the encoded data.
77-sunburst-breadcrumb-brush.stress_test_note: brushed() calls applyDesaturation() on every mousemove with no RAF/throttle, clicked() starts a 750ms transition with no .interrupt() allowing mid-flight conflicts, and concurrent brush drags read d.current while the transition tween is mutating it.
77-sunburst-breadcrumb-brush.cognitive_load_note: Single-view sunburst with 4 well-separated rainbow hues manages 213 nodes cleanly; the unlabeled outer ring's 144 thin leaf segments require hover to identify, and the angular brush ring's affordance is non-obvious without a tooltip or label, but neither issue causes overload in normal exploration.

82-hive-plot-accessible.visual_critic_note: The hive plot renders cleanly with a clear triangular structure, but uses default D3 categorical colors (blue/green/red), the 'Connec' label is clipped at the viewport edge, and the axis labels lack sufficient contrast with the background.
82-hive-plot-accessible.encoding_integrity_note: Hive plot uses honest categorical color and fixed-size node encoding with no baseline or lie-factor violations, but radial position maps raw pixel values directly instead of through a D3 scale (no d3.scaleLinear with data-driven domain), making it brittle for real data.
82-hive-plot-accessible.stress_test_note: No brush/zoom/transition interactions to trigger update storms, stale closures, or mid-flight snaps; only minor risk is unthrottled mouseenter→focus link updates and lack of touch/mouse differentiation on mobile.
82-hive-plot-accessible.cognitive_load_note: 3-axis hive plot with 80 nodes and 120 edges is visually manageable — restrained 3-color palette and low edge opacity (0.25) prevent hairball effect — but the 'Connector' axis label is clipped to 'Connec', breaking a key orientation cue.

90-skill-growth-sparklines.visual_critic_note: Functional table with readable sparklines, but entirely undesigned — generic sans-serif, flat typographic hierarchy, default green (#4caf50), sparklines occupy only half the viewport width, and the large empty lower half makes the layout feel unfinished.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.encoding_integrity_note: Area baseline correctly anchored at y=0 (domain [0,100], y0=innerHeight), key function present for object constancy on sort, fixed [0,100] domain is semantically appropriate for skill scores, no lie factor or dual-axis issues.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.stress_test_note: Interactions are limited to click-based column sorting with no brush, zoom, transitions, or cross-view dispatch, making all major stress-test failure modes (update storm, infinite loop, stale closure, mid-flight snap, touch fight) essentially non-applicable; minor inefficiency of full SVG teardown/rebuild per sort click is benign at human click rates.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.cognitive_load_note: 8 rows, single monochrome color, shared y-axis domain (0–100), and compact sparklines form a clean scannable table with minimal cognitive demand.

94-election-swing-map.visual_critic_note: Functional county-level election choropleth with brushable histogram, but no color legend, flat typography, harshly saturated red/blue palette, and the histogram feels visually disconnected from the map — competent but undesigned.
94-election-swing-map.encoding_integrity_note: Histogram zero baseline and linear color scale are correct, but the Y-axis domain recalculates from d3.max per year, causing bar heights to rescale across transitions and breaking cross-year visual comparisons (subset/shift invariant violation).
94-election-swing-map.stress_test_note: The brush handler calls applyBrushFilter() on every mousemove doing a full DOM class-toggle walk over ~3k county paths with no RAF/throttle, and updateView() starts 400ms transitions without .interrupt(), causing mid-flight snaps when the slider is dragged rapidly.
94-election-swing-map.cognitive_load_note: Two-view linked dashboard (choropleth + histogram) with a familiar diverging red/blue political palette stays well within working memory limits; the brush-to-dim linking is clear, but the histogram is small relative to the map and animated county fills across ~3000 paths could feel busy at slower connections.
